title: From Ant to Gradle across ZAP's repositories
description: How the zaproxy, zap-extensions and zap-core-help builds moved from Ant to Gradle in 2019, as recorded in the repository history.

chapters.title: An Ant build from the 1.0.0 era
chapters.text: The commit titled "Version 1.0.0" (2010-09-04) adds build/build.xml, an Ant build file.

chapters.title: Gradle tasks appear alongside Ant
chapters.text: On 2016-07-21 a commit titled "Add Gradle tasks to build/publish zap-2.5.0.jar" adds build.gradle. The Ant build file is still present at that point.

chapters.title: zap-core-help sets up Gradle first
chapters.text: On 2019-02-08 zap-core-help gets "Initial set up to build the add-ons", its first Gradle build. No Ant build file (build.xml) appears anywhere in that repository's history.

chapters.title: zap-extensions drops Ant on 2019-04-03
chapters.text: zap-extensions had an Ant build file from its first commit (2011-12-12). On 2019-04-03 the commit "Remove Ant build and set up Gradle build" removes it and adds the Gradle build. The add-ons are then relocated into their own projects, one commit each, starting minutes later.

chapters.title: zaproxy follows on 2019-05-22
chapters.text: On 2019-05-22 the commit "Remove Ant build and set up Gradle build" deletes build/build.xml and adds build.gradle.kts. Shortly afterwards "Add zap project" adds zap/zap.gradle.kts, the module that holds the core sources today.
